To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the psychometric evidence for most needs assessment instruments for dementia caregivers is insufficient and that further development is needed, particularly regarding the structural and construct validity of the instruments.
the psychometric properties of needs assessment instruments used for informal dementia caregivers living with dementia are limited.

the needs assessment instruments for caregivers of people with dementia have limited psychometric evidence and need further developments in the area of validity, reliability, and sensitivity to change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development, validation, and application of a new questionnaire for the assessment of needs of caregivers of people with dementia (the Caregivers' Needs Assessment Scale, CNAS).
the needs of informal caregivers of people with dementia and the development of a new questionnaire for the assessment of these needs.
the development and validation of an instrument for the comprehensive assessment of the needs of informal caregivers of people with dementia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
none of the reviewed instruments is currently ready to be used in clinical practice and research without further development.
there is a lack of a valid needs assessment instrument for informal dementia caregivers.
the "Partnering with better health living with dementia" has the best psychometric properties of the reviewed needs assessment instruments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the "Partnering" instrument has good evidence for content and structural validity and for inter-rater agreement, but lacks evidence for internal consistency.
the needs of informal caregivers are still insufficiently addressed and that there is an urgent need for more reliable and valid instruments to assess the needs of informal carers.
we need a better understanding about what is needed and how needs are defined, measured and assessed in informal dementia caregiving.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development and validation of a reliable and valid needs assessment instrument for informal caregivers is a long and complex process.
the field of needs research for dementia caregivers is in its infancy and that further research is needed to develop a valid and reliable needs assessment instrument for clinical practice.

the development and validation of needs assessment instruments should follow the guidelines and recommendations for developing and validating patient reported outcome measures, as well as the international recommendations on the use of patient reported outcomes in health assessment.
